learn.title: India ISTS Waiver Policy
learn.intro: India's ISTS waiver policy revolutionized renewable energy by waiving transmission charges for solar and wind projects, slashing costs and accelerating grid integration. This policy reduced inter-state power tariffs by up to 30%, enabling affordable clean energy access across regions and supporting India's 500 GW non-fossil target by 2030.
learn.c1_text: Waiving inter-state transmission charges for renewable projects cut costs by 15-20%. Like removing tolls on a highway, this policy lets solar and wind farms sell power at lower tariffs, making clean energy cheaper than coal in many regions.
learn.c2_text: Waiver policies reduced solar tariffs from ₹7.5/kWh to ₹2.5/kWh in auctioned projects. This mirrors carpooling savings: shared infrastructure costs lower expenses for all, enabling developers to bid aggressively while ensuring grid stability.
learn.c3_text: India's 2024 renewable capacity reached 175 GW, with ISTS waivers enabling 90 GW solar installations. The policy supports 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030, aligning with Paris Agreement goals and reducing fossil fuel dependency by 40%.

learn.title: Second Life EV Batteries
learn.intro: Repurposing retired EV batteries for grid storage tackles waste and energy demand. With 70% of battery capacity retained post-vehicle use, these systems provide affordable grid stability, storage, and backup power, crucial for integrating intermittent renewables into global energy systems.
learn.c1_text: EV batteries retain 70-80% capacity after 8-10 years. Like recycling plastic bottles, used batteries are tested, reconditioned, and deployed for stationary storage, extending their lifecycle and reducing e-waste by 30%.
learn.c2_text: Second-life batteries store excess solar/wind energy during low demand, releasing it during peaks. Their 3-5 MWh capacity rivals small power plants, offering fast-response grid services like frequency regulation and microgrid support.
learn.c3_text: Europe leads with 1.5 GWh annual second-life battery deployments (2023). Companies like Nissan repurpose Leaf batteries for UK grid projects, cutting storage costs by 40% compared to new batteries while supporting 20% renewable energy targets.

learn.title: Hydrogen Fuel Cells
learn.intro: Hydrogen fuel cells generate clean electricity by combining hydrogen and oxygen, producing only water as waste. With 60% efficiency in vehicles, they offer zero-emission transport for heavy industries and long-haul trucks, complementing solar/wind by storing excess renewable energy as hydrogen.
learn.c1_text: Hydrogen ions (H+) and electrons separate at the anode, creating electricity. Like a waterfall, this flow powers vehicles silently, with water vapor as the sole byproduct—ideal for cities aiming for net-zero emissions by 2050.
learn.c2_text: Fuel cells enable 500 km range refueled in 3 minutes. Toyota Mirai and Hyundai Nexo achieve 60% efficiency, outperforming batteries in cold weather. Their 100% recyclable components support circular economy goals.
learn.c3_text: Germany's 900+ hydrogen refueling stations (2024) support 10,000 fuel-cell vehicles. Projects like H2Haul target 1.5 Mt of hydrogen transported annually for steelmaking, reducing industrial CO2 by 95% compared to coal.

learn.title: Wave Energy Converters
learn.intro: Wave energy converters harness ocean motion to generate electricity, tapping into 2 PW of global theoretical potential. Technologies like oscillating water columns and point absorbers convert wave kinetic energy into power, offering predictable renewable energy to coastal regions with 40% capacity factors.
learn.c1_text: Oscillating water columns use wave motion to drive turbines, while point absorbers convert vertical movement to electricity. Like underwater windmills, these systems achieve 70% efficiency in converting wave energy to grid power.
learn.c2_text: Marine environments demand corrosion-resistant materials and subsea cables. Projects like Portugal's WaveRoller use modular designs to connect to substations via 33 kV cables, ensuring stable 1-2 MW output per unit with 90% reliability.
learn.c3_text: Australia's Perth Wave Energy Project targets 10 MW by 2025, powering 5,000 homes. Scotland's MeyGen uses tidal stream tech for 6 MW, proving wave energy's viability in high-energy zones with 12-hour daily wave cycles.

learn.title: Agrivoltaics Farming
learn.intro: Agrivoltaics combines solar panels with crop production, maximizing land use while boosting farmer incomes. Elevated panels reduce water evaporation by 30%, increase crop yields by 20-60%, and generate dual revenue streams—critical for sustainable food-energy systems in drought-prone regions.
learn.c1_text: Elevated panels (2-4m high) allow machinery access while shading crops. Like a parasol for plants, they reduce heat stress, increasing vegetable yields by 60% and cutting irrigation needs by 25% in arid zones.
learn.c2_text: Farmers earn 15-30% more per hectare via electricity sales. In France, agrivoltaic farms achieve €12,000/ha annually vs €8,000 for crops alone, with 20-year power purchase agreements ensuring stable income.
learn.c3_text: Gujarat's 5 MW agrivoltaic project powers 3,500 homes while irrigating 200 acres. Similar to Japan's 100 MW initiative, India's model integrates drip irrigation with solar, reducing water use by 40% and yielding 2x income for farmers.

learn.title: Bifacial Solar Panels
learn.intro: Bifacial panels generate power from both sides, boosting energy output by 20-30% through albedo effects. By capturing reflected sunlight from ground surfaces, they maximize efficiency in snowy, sandy, or white-covered areas, reducing levelized costs by $0.02/kWh compared to traditional panels.
learn.c1_text: Transparent back sheets allow rear-side light absorption. Like wearing sunglasses that reflect light back, panels gain 15-25% more output in high-albedo environments (e.g., snow with 80% reflectivity), enhancing winter performance.
learn.c2_text: Elevated mounting (1-2m) minimizes ground shading. Projects in Spain use white gravel (80% albedo) to achieve 30% higher yields, with 10% lower LCOE. Tracking systems further boost output by 25% annually.
learn.c3_text: China leads with 50 GW bifacial capacity (2024), followed by India's 10 GW target by 2025. UAE's 1.5 GW project uses double-glass panels for desert resilience, achieving 28% efficiency—2% higher than monofacial counterparts.
